text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
FemalePlayer(x) ::: x is a female tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
MalePlayer(x) ::: x is a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
TennisPlayer(x) ::: x is a tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association, then they are one of the most active players in major tennis.
∀x (LostTo(x, igaswiatek) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
∀x (FemalePlayer(x) → LostTo(x, igaswiatek)) ::: All female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (TennisPlayer(x) → (FemalePlayer(x) ∨ MalePlayer(x))) ::: All tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (MalePlayer(x) → LostTo(x, rafaelnadal)) ::: All male tennis players at Roland Garros in 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
(RankedHighly(cocogauff) ∨ LostTo(cocogauff, rafaelnadal)) → ¬MalePlayer(cocogauff) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association or lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is not a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
TennisPlayer(cocogauff) ::: Coco Gauff is at Roland Garros 2022.
Conclusion:
ActivePlayer(cocogauff) ::: Coco Gauff is among the most active major tennis players.
